Remember one sentence: signing a contract is just the beginning, renewal and settlement of claims are where your character is revealed - if the customer still remembers you ten years later, it is the real sales.

This role does not suit people who avoid outreach, struggle with rejection, or need a predictable base salary. Commission-driven earnings fluctuate, and the early years can be difficult before a client base develops.

A common path is: start with a college degree → join an insurance company or a brokerage/agency company → take the insurance qualification exam (such as insurance sales practitioner qualification) → start with personal life insurance or auto insurance, accumulate customers and renew them, and move towards team management, financial planning or high-end customers.

Suitable for people who are mature, resilient and have a strong sense of purpose. If you can withstand rejection and are willing to spend time building customer relationships, there is room for you in this industry.

Insurance Sales Agents (Insurance Sales Agents) sell insurance products to individual and corporate customers, completing the entire process of demand analysis, plan design, insurance application and claims assistance. Their income is mainly based on commissions and performance bonuses. They are the sales positions in the insurance industry that directly face customers and rely most on trust relationships.

paragraphs: A 7/10 score indicates moderate-high AI exposure, with rapid automation of data collection, proposal generation, price comparisons, and sales coaching. Relationship building and accountability remain human responsibilities.

But medium to high exposure does not equal high risk. Precisely because the threshold has been leveled by AI and sales are forced to "be better at managing relationships and understand complex needs", consultative sales are actually more valuable. Those who are really being squeezed are the bottom-level salespeople who are pure talkers and rely on poor information, and the retention rate will be further reduced.

If you want to enter the industry, you must first recognize that this is "sales" and not "clerkship": choose finance, insurance, and marketing majors, do more internships during college to accumulate experience in customer communication, and pass the professional qualification exam in advance.

Be familiar with AI solution tools and take the initiative to learn complex products (pension, health, corporate group insurance). From "talking sales" to "consultative management", managing the customer pool and renewing the chassis is more important than filling orders.

Career changers with a sales or service background can get started quickly and focus on acquiring customers and renewing contracts in the early stage. On your resume, write more hard indicators such as "number of customers served, renewal rate, and referral ratio." Don't just write down the amount of performance.

Don't just look at eloquence when recruiting and selling, but also look at demand analysis capabilities and customer management ideas. People who can use AI tools to quickly come up with solutions and explain complex needs thoroughly have a much higher retention rate than those who can only memorize words.

This industry is suitable for people who enjoy "turning strangers into trust" - your customer pool and reputation are compound interest assets that get bigger and bigger.

The charm of this industry is that "people connections are assets" - your customer pool, referral network, and reputation are the capital you accumulate more and more. People who like to deal with people, can handle performance pressure, and enjoy the moment of closing a deal will find a sense of explosion here.
